title: Casper and the Gravity
premise: Ines Dunmore, a xenolinguist who once translated the first contact protocols and now hauls cargo to stay forgotten, discovers their own name on the manifest of the Meridian, a ship that officially never flew—and that supposedly died with everyone aboard, including Ines. The manifest is a forgery, but a perfect one, built from the sealed records only Ines and one other survivor could know: Commander Sefa Okonkwo, who now commands half the fleet hunting for proof the Meridian's last transmission was falsified. That falsified transmission is the only thing keeping two fleets from open war, and someone is using Ines's stolen identity to unravel it. To keep the lie alive, Ines must reconstruct what really happened on the Meridian—memories they've spent three years refusing to dream about—and finally choose between preserving the peace built on their erased survival or telling a truth that will burn both fleets down.
about_author: Emrys Eastwick is a former shipping-logistics analyst who spent six years writing route reports for orbital freight companies before turning those ledgers into fiction. They write quiet, bureaucratic science fiction about people whose lives are measured in manifests, margins, and things left unsaid.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A routine cargo run through contested orbit establishes Ines's careful invisibility: no dreams in human languages, no names given twice, no history. When docking control flags an anomaly—a ship registered to them that never existed—the chapter ends on cold dread. Emotional beat: the cost of hiding exposed as fragile.

chapters.title: The Manifest
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines pulls the Meridian's manifest and finds their own name listed among the dead, dated after the disaster. The forgery is flawless, using details only two living people could know. Flashback fragments hint at the crash Ines survived alone. Emotional beat: vertigo—the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, with an interlude from fleet analyst Dario Voss. We learn the stakes: the Meridian's final transmission blamed a navigation fault, not a weapons test, and both fleets accepted the lie as the price of ceasefire. Someone circulating the forged manifest threatens to reopen everything. Emotional beat: dawning scale of danger.

chapters.title: Sefa
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines seeks out Commander Sefa Okonkwo, the other survivor, expecting an ally. Instead Sefa receives them coldly, denies everything, and warns them off—but her hands shake when she says the Meridian's name. Emotional beat: betrayal and old intimacy curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Cargo of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Dario Voss's POV. Dario traces the forged manifest through freight channels and closes on Ines, believing them either a fraud or a ghost. He reports to Admiral Kettering, who wants the Meridian question buried—or weaponized. Emotional beat: hunter closing in, sympathy complicating pursuit.

chapters.title: What the Dream Said
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Sleepless, Ines finally dreams in human language for the first time in three years: the Meridian's bridge, Sefa's voice counting down, a choice made in seconds. Ines wakes knowing the official story is wrong—and that they told it. Emotional beat: memory returning like a wound reopening.

chapters.title: The Third Name
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Digging deeper, Ines finds a third name on the original crew list, redacted everywhere: Jun Okafor, the communications officer whose signature authenticates the fatal transmission. Jun's body was never recovered. Emotional beat: the lie has a missing author.

chapters.title: Interrogation at Dock Nine
chapters.summary: Alternating Ines/Dario POV. Dario detains Ines under identity-fraud statutes; Ines talks circles around him in four languages, buying time but confirming his suspicion. Kettering orders Ines released—under watch—as bait. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse with grudging mutual respect.

chapters.title: Sefa's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Sefa summons Ines privately and nearly tells the truth: the transmission was doctored under orders, by both fleets' high commands, to prevent war. She stops short of naming who gave the order. Emotional beat: shared guilt, trust rebuilt one inch at a time.

chapters.title: The Archive Ship
chapters.summary: Ines and Sefa's POV, alternating. They infiltrate a decommissioned archive vessel holding the Meridian's raw flight data, dodging Kettering's patrols. Inside, they find evidence Jun Okafor recorded the real transmission before dying. Emotional beat: desperate hope, tightening noose.

chapters.title: Jun's Voice
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The recovered recording reveals Jun discovered the weapons-test cover-up and was ordered silenced; the 'crash' was engineered. Ines realizes their own survival was permitted only because they were believed dead—and useful as a legend. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into fury.

chapters.title: Kettering's Gambit
chapters.summary: Admiral Kettering's POV. Kettering, author of the cover-up, learns the archive was breached and moves to destroy both the evidence and the survivors, framing the second fleet for sabotage. Emotional beat: antagonist fully revealed—cold, principled, terrifying.

chapters.title: Running Silent
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines and Sefa flee in Ines's cargo hauler, dark-running through contested orbits Ines knows better than anyone. Dario, ordered to hunt them, hesitates—he's found discrepancies in Kettering's logs. Emotional beat: fugitive intimacy between Ines and Sefa; Dario's loyalty cracking.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Cornered and low on air, Ines confesses to Sefa the full truth of the crash: Ines obeyed the order to transmit the false story, trading silence for life. Sefa's forgiveness is not simple. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh—survival as complicity.

chapters.title: Defector
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. Dario confronts Kettering with the log discrepancies and is arrested for it. He escapes with help from a junior officer and sends Ines a coded warning: Kettering has scheduled a 'joint exercise' designed to manufacture an incident. Emotional beat: the bureaucrat becomes a rebel.

chapters.title: Broadcast Rights
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The plan forms: use the Meridian's original frequency and Jun's authentication codes—which only Ines can verify linguistically—to broadcast the truth to both fleets simultaneously before the exercise begins. But broadcasting means revealing Ines is alive, voiding the amnesty that protects them. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Exercise
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Both fleets maneuver toward the manufactured incident; Kettering's trap springs early when Sefa is captured boarding the relay station. Ines must choose: flee with the evidence intact or broadcast incomplete proof to save Sefa. Emotional beat: crisis forcing the central choice.

chapters.title: Climax: The Frequency
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. From the relay station, Ines broadcasts Jun's recording and their own testimony—naming themselves as the voice of the false transmission—in flawless protocol language learned from the aliens who taught them that words are contracts. Both fleets stand down mid-maneuver. Kettering orders fire anyway; her own crews refuse. Emotional beat: catharsis—the lie broken by the liar's own voice.

chapters.title: Aftermath: Arrests
chapters.summary: Dario's POV. Kettering is taken into custody by a joint tribunal; Dario testifies, his career ruined but his conscience intact. Sefa recovers, formally reinstated. Ines, legally dead, watches from the gallery unnoticed. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly, quietly.

chapters.title: Amnesty Refused
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The tribunal offers Ines restoration: name, rank, record. Ines declines—not out of shame, but because the person who earned that record died on the Meridian, and the person who lived should be new. Emotional beat: inheritance examined and set down.

chapters.title: Dreaming Again
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. On a slow haul to the outer stations, Ines dreams—in human language, then in something older and stranger, the contact-language they helped build. Sefa sends word she'll fly with them next run. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted; memory integrated rather than escaped.

chapters.title: Manifest, Final Entry
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, closing frame mirroring Chapter 1. Ines files a new manifest under their own name for the first time in years—one passenger listed: J. Okafor, memorial transit. The name that started everything now carries meaning instead of menace. Emotional beat: the dead carried forward honestly; the arc complete.
